utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Motorolas, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know. I never had a Motorola during the time that I was in the army. I was never issued one. But these were old devices. And if there was a building or there was a hill around, there was interference. The range was greater on flat terrain. So it would vary. I mean, I could give you a -- a sort of layman's view of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, that's okay. I'm grateful for the view you've given. But I'll just ask you one more question: Did you notice very much flat terrain in the Neretva Valley when you were there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no flat terrain there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So the range of these Motorolas in the Neretva Valley was very limited, according to your information.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Apart from those three methods of communication that I've mentioned, are there any others that I've -- that were in existence at the time that I've left out?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're thinking in Jablanica or generally -- well, I can say that another means of communication the army used was through the radio -- ham radio operators, but I don't know whether there was such a connection in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. And by "ham radio operators," you mean effectively private persons who -- who had an interest in radio communications and happened to have a radio set; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was used in Sarajevo quite broadly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But is the situation this: You don't know whether there were such facilities available in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I understand that. Now, I just wanted to ask you now, having gone through that lengthy analysis of communications: You sent your reports to Jasarevic by the paket veza system. What about Brankovic? How did he send his reports to his superiors in Mostar and Konjic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I said that I didn't know whether the MUP used the packet system or whether they used the same one. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Were you present when -- when Brankovic sent his reports off, one of which we have in -- well, perhaps I should -- I'll stop there. I've just presumed something. Do you know whether Brankovic sent one or more than one report to his superiors?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And you were never present when he actually dispatched such a report; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and he wasn't there when I was sending mine out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Okay. To your knowledge, was -- did Sejo Brankovic meet with Minister Alispahic when he came to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was Sejo Brankovic present at the meeting where -- that you've described when Bakir Alispahic was present and there was a discussion about provisions for the troops from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So -- okay. Well, thank you for that. Now, you didn't have a vehicle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As far as you could see, Karic, Suljevic, and Bilajac shared a vehicle, which was driven by the son of Karic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you were effectively dependent upon other persons to give you a lift: For example, Soko, from Zuka's unit, or Sejo Brankovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once. But I didn't even ask that. When we went to Grabovica, I used the car. I was told to sit with Mr. Soko. As far as the other two times are concerned later, I asked Mr. Emin Zebic, because Mr. Brankovic is not from Jablanica. He's from Mostar. So he didn't have any vehicles available. I asked Mr. Zebic to help me out and to lend me a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned there was one occasion when you tried to go to Grabovica but you were turned back at the -- at a checkpoint. Was that one of the times when you had a vehicle loaned to you by Mr. Zebic?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And on that occasion, when you went to that checkpoint, did you have with you your SVB identification card or had you left it behind for the reasons that you explained yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't take it from Sarajevo at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. So just -- I suppose my question is this: When you got to that checkpoint but were turned back by soldiers, you didn't have an SVB card to present to those soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I didn't have it. And I would like to explain. It was a civilian car. It was a Renault 18 of white colour. We didn't use any MUP vehicles. It was just a civilian car of Renault 18 -- a Renault 18 model in white.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Okay. Very well. Now, after the soldiers left for the terrain, you didn't -- sorry, I -- so -- I've got myself confused with two questions. Just pardon me. First of all, as a general proposition, Sejo Brankovic was in your company in the two weeks or so following the killings, and in that time he helped you do the tasks that you were able to do; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In that time, you were -- the tasks that you were actually able to perform really consisted of attempting to gather information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to gather information and send it to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And during that time, you were really waiting for a reply from Mr. Jasarevic to the proposals that you'd made on the 13th of the 9th to put together a commission and to take the other steps that you indicated there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was waiting for somebody to come and assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And during that time of waiting, you had very irregular access to a vehicle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But as far as you could see, the police had goodwill. They were prepared to help you when they did have a vehicle available and they were prepared to -- well, I'll put it step by step. First of all, as far as you could see, the local police acted with goodwill towards you and Brankovic and gave you the assistance as they could; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they assisted us to the extent that it was possible. Let me also stress that the amount of petrol in that area that one could use was restricted and the use of the car as well, so I simply couldn't bring myself to go to them every day and ask for the use of the vehicle. Only in exceptional situations. Because they had a huge fuel crisis as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, did you personally attend at the -- at the left bank of Grabovica and -- and endeavour to speak to any of the refugees there, in this -- and I'm talking now about the two weeks following the killings. Did you go down there and -- and try to speak to any of the refugees?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in those shacks where the refugees were? I never went there and I never attempted to talk to the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. We've heard some evidence about military police -- well, we've heard some evidence from the police, actually, from the civilian police about visits by other persons to that area. Did you become personally aware that some military police people went to the left bank and tried to speak to the -- to the civilians who were still to be found on the left bank?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what about the people who had been evacuated from the left bank? We've heard evidence that some of those had come to Jablanica. Did you speak to any of those people - I mean the Croat people - who had come to Jablanica and make inquires of them as to what they saw, if anything, and what they had to say?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only at a later stage did I find out that some people were evacuated -- or rather, that the civilian authorities placed them somewhere in Jablanica. I had no access to them in order to talk to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that the civilian police who were assisting in this inquiry were going to speak to these civilians?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was my opinion, because they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And as far as you could see, the civilian authorities knew about the crimes and were assisting you in your tasks to investigate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember whether you ever got a -- a report from -- or -- "report" sounds rather grand, I know. Did you ever receive any report or any news as to whether any information was gained by the civilian authorities speaking to such refugees? Sorry, I shouldn't use the word "refugees" because that's -- in this context, it has a double meaning. I'll ask that question again. Do you remember whether you heard that the civilian police got any information from the relocated Croats?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever mentioned any talks or statements to me. This is a piece of information that I never had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Can I ask you this: Was it within your information whether the -- whether some of the -- the villagers, Croat villagers, were too scared to talk about what happened?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And was it ever within your information that the Muslim refugees who were still living in Grabovica were also too scared to talk about what had happened? Did you ever hear that?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand you weren't a member of the civilian police force, but you were in Jablanica. What was life like in Jablanica in those days? Well, that's a very general question, I know, but were there very many refugees living in Jablanica at that time?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were quite a few refugees in Jablanica, but for the most part there were people there who had been released from camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And do you recall whether or not Jablanica was shelled by the HVO at that time, during the time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you in Mostar in the day -- before you were summoned to join the team, you were in Mostar. Can you just tell the Tribunal a bit about what conditions were like for the Bosnian population in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. It's not relevant, what the situation was like in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you have to establish the relevance of this piece of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I agree I have to establish the relevance. Part of the Prosecution case is that Mr. Halilovic has got to take the reasonable steps, and the context in which he takes the steps he takes include that - it's the Defence case - that the operation to relieve Mostar was a very important operation and that it had to go ahead because of the humanitarian and military crisis that was facing the people who lived there. In other words, it wasn't open to simply stop the world in order to investigate this crime because something much worse was happening and was about to happen even more. I'm entitled to lead that evidence to establish the -- the need for this operation to go ahead, because the Prosecution make a criticism of Mr. Halilovic, or I presume at the end of the case will make such a criticism. Well, the Defence is going to say that those in authority, whether the Court is prepared to find that Mr. Halilovic was one such person is another question, but whether he was or he wasn't, those in authority were fully entitled to go ahead with the operation, and we have -- we want to establish that and we want to establish why. And therefore, the situation in -- in Mostar seems to me -- well, I submit it's directly relevant to the questions that are before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the subject matter of this trial is not about any military operations at all. Even if there's a very urgent situation required for the -- the military operations, it has nothing to do with the humanitarian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Here, the subject matter is whether civilians or those who laid down their arms were mistreated or injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, when Mr. Halilovic is charged on the basis of command responsibility, as he is, for failing to punish -- failing to follow up, effectively, in the way that the Prosecution wants to establish, the Court simply can cannot ignore and the Tribunal -- in my in my submission - I don't take Your Honour to mean this, but I have to spell it out clearly - that the context in which Mr. Halilovic is supposed to have taken the actions that the Prosecution want him to take is relevant. It's one thing to say that a commander who is -- who is simply sitting in a command post somewhere in peacetime and learns of a crime and doesn't act has got a certain level of responsibility is one thing. To say that Mr. Halilovic is obliged to take particular steps in the circumstances in which he found himself is quite another. And it must be and will be directly relevant to his culpability here. And the third element of Section 7(3) makes it quite plain that it's the real -- he's got to take all reasonable steps, all realistic steps. And the concept of what's reasonable and realistic is all about the facts. It's not a university exam here. It's a -- it's a real-life situation. Now, if Mr. Halilovic was in the middle of drowning and failed to take certain steps, he wouldn't be guilty. If Mr. Halilovic was being shot at and failed to take certain steps, he wouldn't be guilty. And if he's in the middle of a military operation, then we say he wouldn't be guilty. But it's a question of degree, because, of course, if he's in the middle of a camp where he's busily liquidating many people or being part of such a -- a situation, well, he can say it's a crisis, and it probably is, but he'd still be guilty. But in the middle of a military operation, Your Honour, that's something that you would, in my submission, take a great deal of notice of when deciding whether he had taken all reasonable steps, whether he'd done what was reasonably required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that is a statement in the opening statement or in the closing arguments later on. Here we are going to deal with some practical matters. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the fact that crimes occurred during military operations is why we are here at this Tribunal. Those things happen every single day -- happened every single day in the former Yugoslavia, or happened quite often in the former Yugoslavia. That is not a defence if it occurs in a military operation. We have information concerning a military operation which is underway. We've had evidence of the testimony of the conditions in Sarajevo and Jablanica. There is no need to delve into the conditions in Mostar. We can go off on other tracks and we can spend more time and waste more time on things like this. There just isn't any need. It's not relevant, and I'd ask that they just move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, in this situation, you may ask general questions about, you know, what was happening in Mostar, but I hope you do not go into the very details on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me just ask you a general question: What was the situation like in Mostar for the civilian population when you were there in the week -- weeks leading to your joining the inspection team?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Critical.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In what way critical?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a small area there were many civilians who were refugees from Nevesinje, Gacko, and that part of Herzegovina, and on the one side we had Chetniks, on the other side, the HVO. They were being shelled on a daily basis. They didn't have enough food or water or electricity or medicines. I myself personally witnessed a surgery without anaesthetics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was the military situation like, apart from --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. Now we're into the military situation there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's a little bit far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just persist though. I -- I just want the Prosecutor to clarify this. Do they seriously suggest - and I want this on record - that the military situation is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this should be outside this witness. The witness should be removed if they're going to start to talk about situations in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I haven't heard -- I haven't heard the question put by Mr. Morrissey, so I'm in a difficult position, you know, to say anything at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I -- may I -- I assist here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I want to ask this question. I've -- Your Honours have given me leave, I think, to ask a couple of general questions. I've asked one general question, and now I'm going to ask another one, and then that will be the end of it. But the military situation in Mostar is plainly a matter of relevance. No one objected when I asked questions of those witnesses concerning the Zenica meeting about the urgent situation in Mostar. I've asked the -- these questions of many other witnesses without objection. Now we've got someone who was actually there. In my submission, this is the very witness who can say what situation -- what the situation was in short, brief terms, and it would assist the Tribunal. It's relevant to the third element of 7(3). I'd just ask to persist with that question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may ask this question. But later on we'll consider whether we give any weight to that piece of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course. As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. You've answered the question about the -- the critical situation for the civilians in Mostar. Just tell us, from your experience, what was the military situation facing the government army in Mostar at the time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the military shared in the fate of the civilians. They were on the front lines with a few weapons, very little ammunition, and the only communication lines open to these units were precisely the route I travelled, 18 hours on the road, and it was impossible to provision the army with anything significant in order to make it possible for them to defend themselves. People were exhausted because of combat operations, daily shelling, and we were on the front line all the time. We used to have our meals there, sleep there, because there was nowhere else to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Just excuse me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness now please be shown MFI235. That completes the questions concerning Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm now going to show you your next -- the next report that you -- that you compiled. This is a document that was dated 29 September 1993, and it's the report where you included the list of -- of people who used to live in -- in Grabovica. Do you have that document in front of you yet?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this -- I've got a series of questions about this document. First of all, it's -- it's -- the address at which it's said to have been written is the IKM at Jablanica, on the 29th of September, 1993. And I just want you to -- I just want to ask you a couple of questions about that: To your knowledge, the combat operations involving the Sarajevo units -- I'm sorry, I've been asked to slow down for the interpreters here. Pardon me. The combat operations involving the Sarajevo units ended on or about the 20th of September, and those units then went back to Sarajevo. Is that -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat operations finished and the units went back to Sarajevo, but I can't recollect the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, look, we've heard evidence -- I just want to put this -- we've heard evidence from other witnesses about this. One witness named Okovic tendered a particular document, a record of -- of movements of his unit. Now, if it be the evidence of Mr. Okovic that the units did return on or about the 20th of September, you don't quarrel or dispute that evidence, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness just said he doesn't know when the incidental occurred. Now they're asking him about what some -- what another witness said about something he doesn't know about, and they're asking him if he's disputing it. It's just speculation, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, how do you know that that witness said he doesn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because he just said he doesn't know -- answer: "Combat operations finish and the units went back to Sarajevo, but I can't recollect the exact date." Now they're asking him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The witness said that he did not know about the exact date. Maybe in a certain period. It's within September or the beginning of October? Maybe he could give us a -- a range of dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases. I'll ask the witness about a range of dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, do you agree that -- to the best of your memory, the units from Sarajevo went back to Sarajevo a little under two weeks -- approximately two weeks after the killings took place? Does that accord with your memory or not?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a fortnight, maybe a couple of days longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. At all events, by the time you came to write this particular note, the troops had already been gone back to Sarajevo for a number of days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've already seen -- the Prosecution showed you, I think, a report by the inspection team that was dated the 20th of September? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, is it your recollection that the troops -- that the members of the IKM -- members of the inspection team, in particular -- went back to Sarajevo at approximately the same time as the troops went back?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about it, but I do know that they left before I -- before I did, because I didn't see them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you remained in Herzegovina in your capacity as an SVB operative with the job of looking into the killings at Grabovica to the extent possible; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed at Jablanica for the simple reason that I have no -- I had received no orders to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. But you understood that your -- your obligations concerning the -- the investigation into the -- the killings were ongoing obligations, which included writing this report dated 29 September 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Everything I uncovered in the course of the period of time that I was there and was in any way related to that -- well, I gathered all the information and then I included it in my final report, and that was my final report from Jablanica. And then in the end, since I received no orders to go back, I went back to Sarajevo on my own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And -- well, that was going to be my next question. To the best of your memory, you went back to Sarajevo without receiving any particular order from General Jasarevic; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just have to ask you about that, because we've had evidence from other witnesses in this case, and I just wanted to ask you: Is it possible that you did receive an order from General Jasarevic and you've just forgotten about it now? I'm not telling you what the answer is, yes or no, but I just ask you to consider that. Is it possible that you were told to come back by General Jasarevic and you've just forgotten that request, or do you say that you just were never told and you came back on your own initiative altogether?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how was he supposed to tell me to go back? If I may ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, of course you may ask. There's if -- it's been said that there was a written order for you to come back to Sarajevo. Now, do you recall receiving any such written order?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I never received such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just excuse me a moment. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just -- sorry, pardon me one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, would Your Honours just forgive me an order. I think I might just show that order to the witness just to be fair and make sure that -- that he understands what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry. I'm just going to have -- somebody is going to look for a particular document there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just -- I must say this: I just have the sense -- I don't want to do an unfairness to the witness here. I recall the evidence -- and I may have confused myself as to that particular -- or to any particular document. I just want to research that before I go back to that topic because I don't want to leave the witness in a position of unfairness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Dzankovic, I just want to be clear about that. We had evidence in this Tribunal - that's what I'm putting to you - don't worry about that document that I mentioned for a minute. I'm not so sure about that as I stand here in court questioning you. Anyway, the fact is you've got no recollection of any such request being made. That's the long and short of it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What order? The question you've just asked?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I see on the screen in front of me - and there's a handwritten bit - "Send a telegram to Namik to go back to the security staff," and it is handwritten. But let me reiterate it: I have never ever received any such document, any order in writing from the gentlemen in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just indicate, that's the source of my mistake. The witness has put his finger on it. I had a half memory about it, and so I apologise for wasting the Court's time for five minutes on that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, to come back to this particular document. I just want to ask you about a couple of proposals that are contained in it or suggestions that are contained in it. Do you see there the reference to Samir Pezo?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you just scroll it down a little bit? That's enough. Thank you. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, here you've -- I just remind you of something, that in the previous report you had mentioned the -- the necessity of taking statements from the 2nd Independent Battalion soldiers when they came to Sarajevo. Now, here you were effectively reminding the SVB in Sarajevo that Samir Pezo might have something to say of importance to the investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Samir Pezo was there on the spot; that is to say, in Grabovica, with his unit, and that happened around the area where they were billeted. I suppose that some of his people might have seen something.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. No, I -- I understand. Did you also mention to Jasarevic in the last paragraph that -- an agreement in general terms that the on-site investigation would be done by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, at a meeting -- or rather, when we were trying to arrange things at MUP, we had a conversation about it, since the units had gone away and left the area that there was a possibility to go down there and try to do something. But there was no agreement actually. There was nothing on paper. And I wasn't at a level of somebody who would have been able to agree anything like that or order anything like that. But there were talks about it. As to whether MUP carried out any investigation afterwards or anything, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. And I understand that you were not in a position to give any orders to the MUP. However, it -- when you left Herzegovina, it was your expectation that the MUP would do that job; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I thoughts somebody would have done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And your understanding, because of the conversation you'd -- you had already had, was that it was going to be the MUP who did it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assumed if not MUP, somebody else would be entrusted with the task to do that part of the job, because it is an expert task and quite some time had passed from -- since the killings, that is to say, those events. And as to the investigation and the expert opinion, et cetera, it all requires real experts, especially because quite a bit of time had elapsed since the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And, in fact, you had already given advice way back on the 13th of September that this was what, in your opinion, should be done and should be arranged by your superiors in the SVB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, my final questions relate to the -- the -- and they're very short ones now -- relate to the -- the Operation Trebevic, Trebevic I. When you were -- when you were given your task by military security, had persons already been taken into custody from the 9th and 10th Brigades? Or was that something that was still to occur?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The operation had already begun and people were already brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And were you given anything in writing to indicate the sort of questions that you should ask and the sort of areas that you should explore with the people that you had to interview?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. As to oral instructions, were you told to cover a variety of topics but including the crimes at Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to me specifically but to everyone who had been at the morning meeting such instructions were issued. I never received -- actually, I never had the opportunity to speak to any of the soldiers from the 9th and the 10th, which were in the area of Grabovica at the time of the killings. Others made the schedule, so I never had the opportunity for such an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. No, and I understand you gave that evidence before. But just in terms of -- of the instructions that you were given under Trebevic, who was the person at the morning meeting who gave you your tasks?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Vahid Bogunic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And Vahid Bogunic, can you just explain in terms of the organisation at the UB, which is the -- the highest level of the SVB, what was the relationship of Vahid Bogunic in relation to Jusuf Jasarevic? What was Bogunic's role?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogunic was the number-two man in the security administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you able to say that Vahid Bogunic knew very well that you had been the security person attached to the inspection team that went down to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Had you had any conversations or contacts with Vahid Bogunic between the time when you joined the inspection team and the time when you went to this morning meeting in order to be briefed?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never got in touch with the gentleman, and I did not send my reports to him. I sent my reports to the chief, Jusuf Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. And as you understood -- yes, I withdraw that question. Just one second, please. I've nearly finished this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Just look, my final question is: In that -- in that last -- in the fortnight or so - you've indicated a fortnight or maybe a couple of days more before the soldiers went back to Sarajevo - are you sure you didn't run into Sefer Halilovic down at Donja Jablanica on one occasion after the meeting in the hotel? In other words, after the killings and after the military operation was underway, are you sure you didn't bump into Sefer Halilovic at Donja Jablanica in the company of Zuka on one occasion?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting, as far as I can remember, I did not see Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you ever see his son, Semir, his young son?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Semir was with him when he came to my door. Semir was with him when he came to see me in my room at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Mr. Dzankovic, thank you for your patience in answering the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's the end of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were just discussing the Trebevic number I investigation in the interviews, and you indicated that you didn't interview any members -- I believe of the 9th or 10th, or you might have just said the 9th. Prior to this case in Grabovica, did you have any experience in interviewing homicide suspects?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness answered that question very clearly in evidence in chief. He said "no." I didn't ask him any questions about it at all, and it's not a permissible question at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. This question is asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, but I just -- I think we should be able to go over it because they've just left an impression that they did not use him to interview this -- these certain suspects for the 9th and 10th. And I think they've left a certain impression there. And I think there's a reason why they didn't use him. And I think that's why it's important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Whatever my friend thinks is totally irrelevant. He can ask relevant questions in re-examination according to the rules. And if he's got one, I won't object to it. He can dispel any impression he wants by asking questions within the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that is within the rules. They've raised an impression, which I believe is a false impression, and I'd like to clarify it or correct it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I wish to make --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, you finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. May I just intervene there, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I regret that my friend has now commenced -- he did it yesterday, he's done it today. He's referred to false impressions, and I think yesterday it was said that I misled the witness and so on. I don't want to be defending myself against these comments. I don't mislead witnesses. I don't leave false impressions. I'll clean up anything that needs to be cleaned up, but I want the objection to be made in a proper and fair way without. We don't cast dispersions. I don't want the Prosecutor casting dispersions either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think there's a misunderstanding between the parties on that specific words. Let's come to the specific facts, you know, rather than kind of impression by anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you have any investigative experience with homicide suspects?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about this document number 235, where it talks about the possibility of an on-site investigation and exhumation. Did any member of the inspection team ever request you to perform an on-site investigation or an exhumation at Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, once again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- the learned Prosecutor asked almost verbatim that question in evidence in chief. In cross-examination, I never did put to him or ask him questions about the inspection team asking him to do an on-site investigation of any sort. There's never been any suggestion that they did. The Prosecutor might one day show why they should, but at the moment we're talking about questions arising from cross-examination. And this one just plainly does not. And it's not a question of impressions, dreams, or ghosts. If he points to a question where I raised it, he can clarify it; otherwise, he shouldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that investigation issues is mentioned in the cross-examination. Maybe, Mr. Weiner, you could ask general questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- concerning of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who, if anyone, ordered you to perform an on-site investigation or exhumation at Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive a specific order to that effect from anyone.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Sefer Halilovic requested you to do an on-site investigation or an exhumation process at Grabovica, would you have followed that order?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did I hear my friend refer to the word "speculative" earlier on? Because, Your Honours, this is the sort of question that just cannot be asked. It's speculative. It doesn't arise out of cross-examination. It's -- well, there's all sorts of things I could say about it, but there is no way this question can be asked, and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I respond to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This witness has said at pages 31 and pages 32 that he did not receive any orders from a higher-up -- or from a -- okay. Or if they received an order from a higher-up commander to come, they would have come. And he's referring to an investigative team would have come. If a higher-up commander or if the chief of the military security asked him to come. That's number one. Number two, they've talked extensively about what was done and what was not done. Number three, through his cross-examination, he brought out that Sefer Halilovic was the commander of the I-Team, the inspection team, and that he had given him orders. As a result of those questions, I'd like to ask him: If he had given you an order, would you have followed it? It comes right from the cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the witness answered in his previous answer by saying that nobody gave him any orders to investigate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And we'd like to follow up in a member of the inspection team or Sefer Halilovic gave him an order, would he have followed it as a member of that team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's a very speculative question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, he can say, "I would have followed my commander's question or I would not have followed it."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I hope you could drop this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were asked about your work with the local police department, the local -- with the Jablanica SUP. Did they ever advise you that they took any further -- the local MUP. Did they ever advise you that they took any further statements from any witnesses?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they ever assist you with an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this witness has already said that he didn't perform one. Now, what's the function of that question otherwise than to make a speech? Your Honours, it's -- it's just commentary now and it's not permissible and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware or did they advise you as to the number of Grabovica villagers living in or staying in Jablanica or Donja Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, look, I object to this. I mean, I'm not sure exactly where that's going, but the Prosecutor led in evidence in chief a document where that very list is present. Now, this is simply reiterating evidence in chief. It's not something that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In my submission, this really is reopening evidence in chief at the moment. I'm commenting on the direction of questions generally. That question there seems to be simply reiteration, so I object to it on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, to me the question is another new aspect in that area. I don't think it was raised during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, they -- he asked -- he had asked if he was aware that Zuka had saved any civilians. There's also talk in these reports about other civilians. There's talks about civilians on the left bank and he asked about whether those people were interviewed. My question is: Based on the reports in this case, was he aware of any other witnesses that had left Grabovica and were now living in Donja Jablanica or Jablanica. We've had a lot of testimony about that in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Including the police helping these people go there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: According to a report filed by this witness, about 14 villagers was evacuated after that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Then based on their going through the reports, I'd like to question him about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But this issue was not mentioned during the cross-examination. It should have been done in the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Counsel asked him if he was aware of the civilian police interviewing any other refugees, and then he switched the name from "refugees." This is a lead-off of that. They opened the issue, we're allowed to follow up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, here we have two kinds of refugees. One is a Muslim refugee staying in Grabovica. Another is the refugees with the Croat refugees fleeing from Grabovica to Jablanica. I just got confused on this issue. Maybe Mr. Morrissey could clarify that, because after all, the question was raised by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I actually asked about both. I asked about the ones who came to Grabovica. I asked about the ones who remained in Jablanica. If my learned friend wishes to clarify that matter, then there's no objection to him clarifying whether he knew that there were refugees in Jablanica and whether there were Croats and Muslims, and questions of that nature. I fully concede that my questions there got a little wordy. So I wouldn't object to clarifying about that. As Your Honours pointed out, that's the question I objected to originally, but we might be getting somewhere, so I wouldn't object to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may ask some questions concerning the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that there were refugees from Grabovica, Croatian refugees, staying in Jablanica and Donja Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, one moment I'm not sure there were any staying in Donja Jablanica. I don't think that's evidence at all. I think there's evidence that they were -- they were staying in Jablanica. Donja Jablanica, as I understand, was Zuka's base. And I don't think it's been said there were any refugee there is, and certainly not by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking him if he was aware, Your Honour. They've raised the issue of refugees, Croatian refugees leaving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I'm a little confused now. The original question said "Muslim refugees," and now my friend mentions "Croatian refugees." I think -- my friend is allowed to ask the questions, but has to be precision about it. That's why he's allowed to ask it, precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's the pot calling the kettle black, as to lack of precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, no, no, no, I accept lack of precision. I accept lack of precision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well, let's go step by step. First to clarify refugees and later on ask about the Croatian refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware of any refugees, basically persons from Grabovica, currently staying -- or after the incident staying in Donja Jablanica or Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This term "refugees" is for people who lived there and who after the events had pulled out or were evacuated to Jablanica -- well, actually, it's not clear, but people who stayed alive were transferred to Jablanica, according to my information, and they were -- their accommodation was taken care of by the civilian organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: About how many of these Croats from Grabovica were transported to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact number. I know about the two people evacuated by Adnan Solakovic or handed over to the MUP organs. I know about the two boys, the two children. I can't remember the exact number of people and where they were accommodated. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you or anyone else attempt to interview the two children?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Perhaps my friend could ask two questions, rather than one, arising out of that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you attempt to interview the two children?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of anyone from the MUP of Jablanica attempted to interview the two children?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Other than the two persons that Adnan Solakovic told you about, did you attempt to interview anyone in Jablanica of those persons who were -- were transferred out of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone from the MUP at Jablanica attempted to interview those persons who were transferred out of Grabovica and were staying in -- in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if anybody from MUP interviewed them. I didn't know where they were accommodated either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you were also asked about the different communications systems that they had in Jablanica, and you were asked about the various types of implements that were used, ranging from the packet system to radios to Motorolas. Were messengers ever used, meaning human beings, messengers ever used by the army?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean messengers, couriers?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Over long distances. Over short distances? I understand a messenger wouldn't be used from Jablanica to Sarajevo, but what about over a shorter distance?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that couriers, messengers, were used at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, there were some questions concerning the IKM, the forward command post. Who did you see working at that forward command post in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vehbija Karic, Zicro Suljevic, and Mr. Bilajac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were meetings ever held at that forward command post in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were meetings in relation to Operation Neretva held at that forward command post in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, once again, the Prosecutor is endeavouring to do in re-examination what should have been done, if he wanted to, in evidence in chief. I didn't cross-examine about this. The Prosecutor wasn't prepared to raise it in evidence in chief. It's too late now to reconstruct it, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The first question is allowed, that is, "were meetings ever held in the forward command post in Jablanica." But the second is a little bit too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, they questioned him as to the IKM premises and to the extent of the IKM premises and that there was a conference room there, and that's my follow-up question: Were meetings held there, and were meetings as to Operation Neretva? They brought up the issue of conference room. They opened the issue. They've raised the issue in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the witness has already answered the question concerning of the conference room, because he said that the meeting was held there. But as for the specific meeting concerning of the Operation Neretva, I am not quite sure. You may skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. May the witness be shown Exhibit 215, which is also 221, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: They're both MFI. It's -- 215 and 221 is the same document. Whichever one is clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This is not a quarrel here. I presume 221 is the one I showed him. And I presume these questions arise out of cross-examination. It would be best if he's shown the same one that he was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Whichever one is the clearer one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you have the B/C/S in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you go to page 2, beginning with that paragraph: "According to my information, a man called Ivica, a Croatian member ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation] Could you please scroll it down for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The paragraph beginning with: "According to my information, a man called Ivica, a Croatian member of Zulfikar's special purposes unit ...."

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Go -- go back, up. Could you scroll it up a little bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise for this. I'm not sure if it's a technical problem from our point of view, but I think I've got the Brankovic document in front of me here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that I've got the right document. I found that particular paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours -- Your Honours, it's -- it's just not the same on my computer. I'm sorry. I apologise to the Prosecutor for this. I just don't have the -- Sorry, Your Honour. Might I just confer with Mr. Cengic. It's just that I -- this doesn't seem to be the same document, which I think I know quite well and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, maybe we should take a break now and make it straight. We may have a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, would you just excuse me for a moment. I may know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If Your Honours would just grant us -- grant us 20 seconds to see if we can retrieve the technical situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it document 215 or 221?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI215, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Those are one in the same, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- sorry, I've detected what the problem is. The translations of each -- the English translations of each -- of 215 and 221 are slightly different. Now, the reason why that 221 was tendered separately is because 221 has got some -- has got a handwritten addition on the -- on the front, and that's why it was -- that's why it was tendered differently. That's -- that's really why I wanted the same document to be shown, because there are slight differences, it would appear, not -- not necessarily important ones, but slight differences in the English translation, and that's what's caused the problem here. The Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I don't know that it matters very much. I don't want to obstruct. I see why the problem has now arisen. I'd submit the best course would be, really, to show the witness the one that he was shown in cross-examination, because these questions are arising out of cross-examination. The same document ought to be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I haven't heard the question put by the Prosecution, but this document has already been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Shall we working along with this document, if there's any objections or problems, please feel free to stand up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the information that "at the checkpoint at the entrance to the settlement ..." Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: At the barrier at the -- yes. If you could go down to the area where counsel questioned you on, about three sentences down, four sentences down, right after the rape, the woman that had been raped: "The entire Supreme Command's forward command post of Jablanica had been informed about this event." And then -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. The next sentence: "An investigation into the event ascertaining the exact number of people killed, how they were killed, who the perpetrators -- will be jointly conducted by officials of the military security and Ministry of the Interior." Were you involved or did you determine the exact number of people killed?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to obtain the right number with the help of SJB Jablanica, because prior to that I had never been to Jablanica, so I could not know of the number of people, their names, or any other information in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But did you ever make that final determination of the exact number of people killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, again, this is exactly the sort of question that if my learned friend was serious about raising it, he would have raised it in evidence in chief. I certainly didn't question him on this topic, and now we have, in my submission, another attempt to lead evidence in chief in redirect, and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, but the Prosecution has already raised this issue -- this question before. Here is just a clarification for the answers of this witness. So in this aspect, this question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever make that determination, sir?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I've ascertained, everything I found, if it's me you're asking, is indicated in my next report where you have the indication of numbers, names, et cetera. If it is not the final report, if there is any extra information obtained at a later stage, I'm not aware of that information. So what I mean to say is what I've discovered and what information I managed to obtain is included in my report. Because had I obtained any other information at a later stage, I would have included it. But this is what I know. As to whether this is the actual number, the final result, the final outcome of those events, I do not know. What I do know is included in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The next sentence, how they were killed. Did you ever determine how these people were killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour -- well, you can see what's happening here. I object to it. It really is an attempt to just rerun the whole re-exam -- the evidence in chief, and it's not - simply - related to the previous question at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that the witness has given a very comprehensive answer in his previous answer to all your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, but they have spent over one hour on this exhibit alone, over one hour and tried to indicate and have left an impression that these investigations occurred, and they haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, wait a minute. Your Honour, may I just interrupt here for a moment. There's got to be some propriety about objections and about submissions. Now, the Prosecutor has issued effectively there a comment, a statement, and I seem to recall being ticked off by the Prosecutor for -- for saying things in front of the witness. Now, Your Honour can just see on the screen what's happening now. This has got the smell of desperation about it. I submit it shouldn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour. That's uncalled for, and the witness is here. If he wants to say that, let him please ask for the witness to be removed and then he can say this. Now, that's uncalled for, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well, now it's pretty late at this stage. Mr. Weiner, I believe that the witness has answered your question. Let's take a break, and we'll resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just a few more questions, sir. You were questioned on pages 35 and 36 of the transcript concerning the quote that you had to apply strict censorship to the media, and you answered that. What you were -- among your answers were: "What I was thinking of was actually having the information released after an investigation was conducted and proper steps had been taken." Sir, I just want to clarify. Were those things -- were those two things -- did those two things ever occur?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, my friend had better clarify. Is he asking whether the information was released? Then that would be a matter arising out of cross-examination. If he's asking whether -- and you look at the terms of the question here, you'll see it's another question of the exact same kind I've been objecting to or appears to be. My learned -- my learned friend would not be entitled to ask him whether an investigation was conducted and proper steps were taken. He's already tried both of those. One of them, he was overruled in terms of the propriety or otherwise of the investigation, and Your Honours have already ruled on that in examination-in-chief, as I recall. But if the question is whether the information was released later, then of course I don't object to it. But it looks to me as if it's an attempt to have another go at the same old problem. So if it is, then I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, maybe the witness could answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll clarify the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The question concerns the -- the latter part of the -- of the statement. Was an investigation conducted and proper steps taken? Because you indicated that you were -- you -- it was your view to withhold the information until that occurred. Did those things occur?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well, Mr. Weiner, I believe that question is asked and answered already. If you are concerning of the information, you could go ahead. But as for the two last things, the question has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Finally, sir, you testified that you attempted to interview Samir Pezo and Adnan Solakovic and they weren't -- at that point, they weren't willing to talk to you, and you recommended that they be interviewed again in Sarajevo. Did you ever interview them in Sarajevo? Did you ever make any attempt to do so?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of anyone else who did that?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge El Mahdi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Witness, these are just a few points of clarification I'd like to make. The first relates to the fact that runs as follows: Do you think that or do you believe that an order in certain circumstances - in other words, during a war or an armed conflict - is an order that can be given orally and that this order cannot be given in writing?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my opinion - and let me just reiterate that I'm not an expert on military matters - but I believe that an order can be issued orally, without putting it in writing. That's my opinion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in the light of what's been said by Mr. Halilovic when he met you, you said that you met him in the hotel. He came to your door, and he indicated or hinted that you should pursue your investigation. Do you think that this was an order that was given to you by your superior in the army?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and I acted in accordance with that. Yes, and I acted in accordance with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, then, Mr. Karic in the same way told you -- or in the way you contacted each other, he used words which were quite subtle, and I'm quoting you in English -- you were quite subtle -- [In English] "Do your best and continue to collect as much information as you can" -- [Interpretation] But as far as you were concerned, this was also an order, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An order -- an order has to be followed up upon, doesn't it? In other words, you should then report back to your superior commander or the person above you when he's asked you to do something, because if I understand your testimony well, it's a matter of saying that you reported the information back to your commander; in other words, Mr. Jasarevic, and you didn't report back to either Mr. Karic or Mr. Halilovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I used to submit my reports to my superiors in MUP, but the possibility of letting Mr. Halilovic and Mr. Karic and the others from the inspection team know, it was not within my power. I didn't have the possibility to get to know them, because they were far away in the area of combat operations, so I had no access to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But were you or not a member of that team?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, it was quite reasonable -- or a reasonable thing for them to do to believe that you had the possibility to contact them directly.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the possibility of direct contact did not exist. I was at Jablanica, and the team members were in the area of combat operations tens of kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, was nobody at the advance command post? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And in Sarajevo, couldn't you contact these people, or couldn't you send them your reports?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where in Sarajevo? I don't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For instance, what kind of position did Mr. Halilovic hold, for instance?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was -- he was the Chief of Staff of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So Chief of Staff is a fairly well-known person. If you don't know where his headquarters -- you didn't know where his headquarters were in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I went back to Sarajevo, I was unable to contact Mr. -- he wasn't in Sarajevo. He was in the area of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But nevertheless there were people on duty, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where exactly? I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that he was Chief of Staff. Don't you believe that the Chiefs of Staff have headquarters?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So my question is a very simple one: Were you unable -- materially speaking, were you unable to contact him in his headquarters?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got in touch with the security administration, and they are a part of the Chief of Staff. And I thought that it was up to them to forward it within the structure of their organisation, within the Chief of Staff, where this information was meant to go, because they are a part of the Chief of Staff structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But there are two questions here. The first one is: You were a member of that team, and Mr. Karic, for instance, was also a member of that team, and the chief was Mr. Halilovic; right?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall move on to another question. You said that when you arrived in Donja Jablanica you met the members of that team, with the exception of Mr. Halilovic, who was away, and the Minister of the Interior was also present, as well as the head of the municipality in question; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not at Donja Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where is it, then?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jablanica. Well, so you discussed questions relating to logistics; in other words, the president of the municipality had said that he would supply you with food. Is this true? Is this right?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The agreement was that him and the commander of the brigade would make an attempt at ensuring that there was some food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But before that, before that meeting, nothing had been decided prior to that relating to the accommodation of the troops, where the troops were to be stationed in Grabovica, for instance, and nothing had been decided as far as their food was concerned, and it is at this meeting that these things were decided; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As to accommodation, I'm not aware of that. And this is not something that was discussed at that meeting. Accommodation was not discussed. Just food. And the units had already arrived, and they were in Grabovica that morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But nobody thought of bringing up the issue of accommodation?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, I really don't know who made the decisions pertaining to accommodation and all that. I don't know whether those decisions had been made previously. I only attended one meeting, the one that we are discussing now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. So you said that when you yourself went to Grabovica, you saw members of -- members of this group sleeping in sleeping bags.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who had sleeping bags used them; others used blankets, and others were sleeping on the grass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, one had reason to believe that this had been planned beforehand, that these men were going to be spending the night or a part of the following day in the open air, as they had been given sleeping bags.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those who had sleeping bags were carrying them. Because as I've said before, only very few people had sleeping bags. They brought them from Sarajevo, obviously the ones that had sleeping bags.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
