utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, these were men coming from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 13th of September, you made a number of proposals, but looking at this report it seems that you have not mentioned the fact that members of the 10th Brigade could have been involved in these events. Do you exclude that possibility, i.e., the fact that they could have been involved in these events? A, were they present at the time?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were at Jablanica. They arrived together with those units. As to whether at Grabovica on the spot when I went down there whether there were any members of the 10th Brigade, I cannot tell with any degree of certainty, because there was nothing on their uniforms for me to be able to tell what unit they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But in your report, you don't allude to the 10th Brigade at all. You talk about the 9th Brigade, the commander of the 9th Brigade. You mention the 2nd Independent Brigade [as interpreted] also. But you don't mention the 10th Brigade at all, which may tend to indicate that at the time you drafted your report it didn't even cross your mind. In other words, you didn't even think that they may have been present.

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that they came to Jablanica. So they came with those units. As to where they were housed or whether they were in Grabovica, I had no way of telling, because their commander at the time did not leave Sarajevo. Had he been there, in all probability I would have been able to know and to find out whether they were there or not. But I repeat once again: They had no insignia on their uniforms, and I had information that a part of the 9th, a part of the 10th, and a part of the independent battalion had left Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. [In English] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's questions? I see -- no? Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just a few.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Further.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did someone tell you that the 10th was going to be arriving?

utterances.speaker: NAMIK DZANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the 10th Brigade. I heard that a part of the 10th, a part of the 9th Brigade, and a part of the Independent Battalion would come.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, who told you that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That doesn't arise out of Judge El Mahdi's question in the least, with respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that Judge El Mahdi's question mentioned that -- the presence of the 10th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So -- so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As to who told. But anyway, if it's going to assist the Court, I won't persist with the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember who exactly told me. Quite simply there was talk about the fact that units from Sarajevo, parts of those brigades were supposed to come from Sarajevo. But who exactly told me, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, there -- there may be a translation issue. It's not something that needs to be -- needs to trouble the Court -- or the witness, frankly. We'll seek a clarification of it at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So -- otherwise, nothing arising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, at this stage, is there anything to tender. Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. There are a group of MFI documents, MFI215, 225, 235, 232, and 130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, are they admitted already?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, they're all pending admission. Most of them are Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I wasn't sure if ours had already been admitted in. MFI282 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. Well, MFI283 might have been admitted already. Yes, Your Honours, as to those other ones that my learned friend Mr. Weiner has referred to, there's no objection to them. I think that the position with those that they were admitted. I thought they were admitted already, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, but since you are no --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not objecting in the least, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But it's just that there's a lot of these -- these documents which we -- perhaps we need to have a -- a little talk with the Prosecutors and clean it up. We don't object to the ones that are offered here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. So those documents are admitted into the evidence. On the part of the Defence, are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. Madam Usher will show you out of the room, and we wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So, Mr. Re, I believe that the next witness is ready for testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ahmed Kaliman. I call him as the Prosecution's next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Or good afternoon. Well, could you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Kaliman, your name is Ahmed Kaliman, and you were born on the 6th of July, 1971. Your current occupation is unemployed. And in 1993, you were a member of the assault or reconnaissance group of the 9th Motorised Brigade in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we don't want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- Object as early. But I think the term used by my friend should be clarified. The two units, the assault and reconnaissance are actually two different entities, and that should be made very clear to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I'm indebted to my friend. I'm sure that the witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well -- you have to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, my information from the witness in my proofing was that it was called the sabotage/reconnaissance brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may put this question to the witness directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's go back to the beginning. Your name is Mr. Ahmed Kaliman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And your date of birth, the 6th of July,1971.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you unemployed?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In 1993, were you a member of the 9th Motorised Brigade in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the name of the -- the group in which you were a member of within the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Reconnaissance assault unit -- company.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that the same as a sabotage brigade or unit?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does that clarify it sufficiently for Mr. Mettraux's purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to the Prosecution for the clarification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Kaliman, I want to show you a statement which I intend to tender under Rule 89(F). I have two copies, one in Bosnian and one in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could these please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please just look at those two documents. Is that the Rule 89 -- is that the statement you prepared based upon your statement to the Prosecutor in 2000 and does it bear your signature on the bottom of each page? Is that the document you signed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is it true and correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The copy to your right, is that the English copy which you also signed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I tender those two statements as the witness's evidence in chief, and in addition I wish to -- or I need to show him three photographs which are in evidence. The purpose -- I have to show them to him because, it being e-court, he has to do it in court, and have him mark on the three photographs, and that will be his evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This document will be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P285.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kaliman, I wish to show you three photographs of things which are referred to in the statement which we have just tendered into evidence. Firstly, in your statement, you referred to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown, I'm sorry, Exhibit P78 -- photograph P78.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your statement, you referred to you and other members of the reconnaissance -- or sabotage/reconnaissance company, as you call it, staying in a house several hundred metres from the main part of the village. What I want you to do is to look at photograph P78, which has some numbers and some arrows. It should be to the left of you, if you look at it. And can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, which house it was, if you can.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: 2, 2a, or -- or 3, 3a. I cannot remember exactly. It's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was one of those three houses; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your statement, you also refer at paragraph 10 to visiting the house where Sejo Karadzic and Haris Karagic was staying that night. Again, is that house marked on that photograph? And if so, can you please just tell us the number of it.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: I don't see a number for it on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Which area was it? There are -- there are houses marked 1 to 9. Was it in the area in which the houses were marked 1 to 9 or was it somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: No, no, it's not in this area. There are two houses that are not marked, and it's one of those two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Are they to the left or the right of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: On the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown photograph P3.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your statement, Mr. Kaliman, at paragraph 16, you refer to Ramiz Delalic lining the soldiers up in the meadow near the river. I just want you to mark on the photograph with the pen, which the court officer will bring to you, with an arrow pointing down to where it was that you were lined up.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: In one of these two locations for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P286.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The final photograph I wish to show you, Mr. Kaliman, is photo P86. I'm going to show you -- it's an overhead photograph of the Grabovica area. And my question relates to photograph 15 of your statement, where you refer to coming to the village entrance and seeing four to six bodies in the bank and on the Neretva River. What I want you to do is look at the photograph to your left there. Can you see in that photograph the area where you saw the bodies.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would you -- would it assist if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we haven't got that picture yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On my screen, I've got the right one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We have it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you have the right photograph now, Mr. Kaliman?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, do you see the -- the place there where -- the place where you saw the bodies? If so, can you please get the pen and mark with a large arrow going downwards, with an arrowhead at the bottom, where the bodies were.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you make -- could you just make the -- make it a bit -- a bit longer, please, the arrow. Just a bigger one, please.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: [Marks] Is this all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I just want to clarify which side of the river the bodies were on. Was it the side which you've drawn the top of the arrow, that is, the red, or was it the other side?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: The bottom of the arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You mean the same side as where you've drawn the arrow? There are two sides of the river there.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: This side where the bottom of the arrow is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is it clear to the Trial Chamber? I can't see whether it's on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, to me it's very clear. How about the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the witness could simply be asked whether it would be on the north side of the river or the south side of the river, or, I mean, as -- on this picture, east or west, I mean, depending on what the witness would prefer. Or to put a dot on the side that he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is it the top -- the top side of the river or the bottom side of the river in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Can I put a dot there? Then that would make things easy for everyone, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. You're indicating, I think, on the bottom side of the photograph, the river-bank on the bottom side, the bottom half of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence too, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no objections, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The Defence is happy with the dot. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P287.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the evidence in chief of this witness. I just wish to read a brief summary of his -- of the contents of his evidence, which will take me about a moment -- a minute to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if there's no disputes about the contents of the summaries, are there any need to read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For the purpose of the public proceedings, I -- that's the -- that's the practice in the Milosevic case, the Krajisnik case, that we read a brief summary so that the public and everyone outside the court knows what -- what the witness has testified about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you insist, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. A brief summary of Mr. Kaliman's evidence is that in 1993, as he said, he was in the sabotage/reconnaissance group in the 9th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you please read more slowly, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Noting that I've given a copy to the interpreters, I certainly will. Everyone in the brigade, including Mr. Kaliman, considered Ramiz Delalic as its commander. He was ordered to Herzegovina in late summer, early autumn 1993, and he travelled to Grabovica with other soldiers from his unit. The reconnaissance group billeted itself in a vacant house several hundred metres from the main part of the village, about 15 to 20 soldiers stayed in that house. On the first day of their arrival, they rested. That night he met Sejo Karadzic - Karagic, sorry - and Haris Rajkic in that house and those two and others came later to Mr. Kaliman's house and ate with them there. On the day of the shooting, he heard shooting coming from different directions. He stayed in the village for at least two days. On possibly the second day, he and another soldier attempted to walk to Jablanica to buy some items. He was stopped at a checkpoint on the way to Jablanica by military police, who ordered them to return to Grabovica. On the way back, neither the entrance to Grabovica, he saw the bodies of about four to six males in civilian clothing lying face down. Two or three were floating in the Neretva River and one or two were half on the river-bank. The bodies had not been there when he walked along the road several hours earlier. After this, Ramiz Delalic lined the soldiers up, asking for volunteers to go into battle. Mr. Kaliman felt depressed by what he had seen and said that he did not want to go into battle. He and the other members of the reconnaissance group left Grabovica for Sarajevo. When the soldiers returned from battle, possibly the same night. He was first questioned about the Grabovica killings in April 2000. That's the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask how long your cross-examination will last, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Probably between five and ten minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to finish your cross-examination, and I apologise for the delay to the -- this afternoon's sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. And we're grateful to the court staff for letting us continue a bit over the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kaliman. My name is Guenael Mettraux and I'm appearing as co-counsel for Sefer Halilovic. You've indicated in your evidence in chief that in September 1993 you were a member of the 9th Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you had joined this particular brigade because it was defending that part or an area of Sarajevo where you came from; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was also the area of the city which you knew best and the area which you were keenest to defend because part of your family was still living in that area; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the time, sir, that brigade was so large that you wouldn't know every single member of the brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What you knew, however, sir, is that within that brigade there were a number of battalions and within those battalions a number of companies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And among those companies within the 9th Brigade were, for instance, a military police company?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. I apologise. There were -- you've indicated that there were a number of companies within the 9th Brigade. I'm going to put to you a number of such companies, and if you could confirm or, if not, indicate whether or not there was such a company within that brigade. And I've indicated to you that there was a military police company within the 9th Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There was also a -- an artillery company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There was also an assault company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There was a logistics company?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There also was a company called the sabotage and reconnaissance company, of which you were a member; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that reconnaissance company, of which you were a member, were made up of approximately 60 men, I think you've indicated in your evidence in chief, at the relevant time, that is, in September of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the commander of that company was a person named Kumbara Dzafer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But Kumbara Dzafer didn't go with you to Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact, most of that reconnaissance company didn't go to Herzegovina with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And, in fact, only 15 or 20 members of that company had been selected within the company to go to Herzegovina, including yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And to lead those 15 or 20 men to Herzegovina, an individual -- I'm sorry, an individual nicknamed Zuti had been selected; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, the real name of Zuti is Mustafa Rustemagic [phoen]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: I know the name, the first name, but I'm not sure about the last name. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you know that this person's first name would be Mustafa; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as far as you know or as far as you can tell, he was the only individual with the nickname Zuti within the 9th Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: It was a large brigade, and there were many nicknames. I can't remember all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But about nickname, sir, this Mustafa Zuti was a different person than Mustafa Hota, known was Musa; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: That's right. It's not the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I have one last question, sir: You've indicated, I think, in your evidence in chief that you didn't go into combat; is that correct? You stayed in the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But a number of individuals from your brigade did, in fact, go to combat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, sir, that within a few days of having left for combat those same individuals came back to Grabovica and that you immediately left for Sarajevo together? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED KALIMAN
utterances.text: We went to Sarajevo together, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That will be all the questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. After we are adjourned, Madam Usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. At this stage, I would like to request the Prosecution to furnish the proofing notes of the next witness before 3.00 this afternoon, if it has been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's already been done, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. So the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
